description:
## Scope

Workspace-architectural sweep deriving from findings filed in two parallel review epics:

- bd:JMAP-ayoz.39 (metadata-server review, P2)
- bd:JMAP-x2gd.93 (chat-server review, P2)

Both findings identify the same workspace-canonical drift: every extension-server handler that extracts a non-`accountId` identifier from wire input uses the unchecked `Id::from(s)` (or `Id::from(s.to_owned())`) constructor instead of the validating `Id::new_validated(s)`. RFC 8620 §1.2 specifies `Id` as 1–255 bytes of SAFE-CHAR `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`; the unchecked path accepts arbitrary content.

Only `accountId` is validated, by `jmap_server::handlers::extract_account_id`.

## Why P2 not P0/P1

The HTTP body-cap is the structural defense (kit-consumer responsibility per workspace AGENTS.md). This finding is defense-in-depth — closes spec non-conformance and per-Id amplification within the HTTP body budget, plus protects downstream consumers that interpolate Ids into URLs/logs/SQL without re-validating.

## Affected sites (per-crate counts as of 2026-05-16)

| Crate | `Id::from` sites | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| jmap-mail-server (canonical) | 35 | identity / email / mailbox / sieve / submission + 2 internal in memory/mod.rs |
| jmap-chat-server | 24 | enumerated in JMAP-x2gd.93 |
| jmap-calendars-server | 10 | |
| jmap-tasks-server | 7 | |
| jmap-contacts-server | 7 | |
| jmap-filenode-server | 5 | |
| jmap-sharing-server | 3 | |
| jmap-metadata-server | 3 | 1 internal (filter_changes_array line 276) + 2 wire-boundary |

**Total ~94 sites.** Per-crate audit will separate wire-boundary sites (need validation) from internal sites (Ids returned by backend; out of scope).

## Decision: fix shape (option a vs b vs c)

The .93 description enumerates three options:

- **(a) Mechanical:** every handler-site `Id::from(s)` → `Id::new_validated(s).map_err(...)?`.
- **(b) Type-system:** remove `Id::From<String>` / `From<&str>` impls, force callers to pick validated.
- **(c) Serde:** `#[serde(try_from = "String")]` on `Id`. Doesn't help direct `.as_str()` extraction paths.

**Recommendation: option (a) first, defer (b) as a follow-up.** Rationale:

1. (a) is mechanical and lands the integrity/availability fix immediately.
2. (b) is a public-API break on the workspace's canonical foundation type (`jmap_types::Id`). Every wire-type struct currently uses `Id::from` internally in its serde `Deserialize` derives; removing the `From` impl forces a serde `try_from` migration on every public struct. That is a workspace-canonical-type API-shape decision separable from the integrity fix.
3. (c) alone doesn't cover direct `.as_str()` → `Id::from` paths, so option (a)'s call-site fixes are needed regardless.

After option (a) lands and the regression-resistance question becomes 'how do we keep new handlers from regressing', file a follow-up bead for option (b) as a workspace-API decision for the human to ratify.

## Per-crate children (canonical first, then siblings)

1. **Canonical:** jmap-mail-server (35 sites)
2. jmap-chat-server (24 sites)
3. jmap-calendars-server (10 sites)
4. jmap-tasks-server (7 sites)
5. jmap-contacts-server (7 sites)
6. jmap-filenode-server (5 sites)
7. jmap-sharing-server (3 sites)
8. jmap-metadata-server (3 sites — 2 in scope)

Each child:
- Audits its sites to separate wire-boundary from backend-return-value usage
- Replaces wire-boundary `Id::from` with `Id::new_validated` and maps the error appropriately:
  - For `/set update` map keys: invalidProperties SetError into notUpdated
  - For `/set destroy` array elements: invalidProperties SetError into notDestroyed
  - For other wire arg fields (`chatId`, `spaceId`, etc.): top-level invalidArguments error
- Adds a per-crate negative test (a request with an invalid Id is rejected, not silently accepted)
- Closes the matching sibling-tracker bead in JMAP-ayoz / JMAP-x2gd scope

## Acceptance

- All 8 child beads closed
- Workspace-wide grep `rg 'Id::from\\(.*str' crate-jmap-*-server/src/` returns only backend-return-value sites (each marked with a comment explaining why it's out of scope)
- Workspace test suite green
- Per-crate negative tests added for at least one wire-boundary site

## Cross-references

- Triggering review beads: bd:JMAP-ayoz.39, bd:JMAP-x2gd.93
- Related: bd:JMAP-6xs8.19 (Id::new_validated character set is wider than RFC 8620 §1.2 — may bite the propagation if validation is tightened mid-sweep)
- Workspace AGENTS.md 'Caller identity (foundation seam)' (backend-canonical, but this is wire-boundary not auth)
- Workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' (mail-server is canonical extension-server)
